arxiv-1912-13002.creator: Gustavo H. de Rosa, Douglas Rodrigues, João P. Papa
arxiv-1912-13002.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Gustavo H. de Rosa, Douglas Rodrigues, João P. Papa. Optimization aims at selecting a feasible set of parameters in an attempt to solve a particular problem, being applied in a wide range of applications, such as operations research, machine learning fine-tuning, and control engineering, among others. Nevertheless, traditional iterative optimization methods use the evaluation of gradients and Hessians to find their solutions, not being practical due to their computational burden and when working with non-convex functions.

arxiv-2212-14214.title: Backward Curriculum Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2212-14214.creator: KyungMin Ko
arxiv-2212-14214.description: Abstract Current reinforcement learning algorithms train an agent using forward-generated trajectories, which provide little guidance so that the agent can explore as much as possible. While realizing the value of reinforcement learning results from sufficient exploration, this approach leads to a trade-off in losing sample efficiency, an essential factor impacting algorithm performance.

arxiv-2306-01702.description: Abstract A Boolean ring and its Stone space (Boolean space) are primitive if the ring is disjointly generated by its pseudo-indecomposable (PI) elements. Hanf showed that a primitive PI Boolean algebra can be uniquely defined by a structure diagram .

arxiv-2401-13671.title: Determinants of renewable energy consumption in Madagascar: Evidence from feature selection algorithms
arxiv-2401-13671.creator: Franck M. Ramaharo and Fitiavana M. Randriamifidy
arxiv-2401-13671.description: Abstract The aim of this note is to identify the factors influencing renewable energy consumption in Madagascar. We tested 12 features covering macroeconomic, financial, social, and environmental aspects, including economic growth, domestic investment, foreign direct investment, financial development, industrial development, inflation, income distribution, trade openness, exchange rate, tourism development, environmental quality, and urbanization.

arxiv-2503-00777.title: A two-dimensional semiconductor-semimetal drag hybrid
arxiv-2503-00777.creator: Yingjia Liu, 1,2,3 Kaining Yang, 4,5 Kenji Watanabe, 6 Takashi Taniguchi, 7 Wencai Ren, 1,2† Zheng Vitto Han, 3,4,5† and Siwen Zhao 3†
arxiv-2503-00777.description: Abstract Lateral charge transport of a two-dimensional (2D) electronic system can be much influenced by feeding a current into another closely spaced 2D conductor, known as the Coulomb drag phenomenon – a powerful probe of electron-electron interactions and collective excitations. Yet the materials compatible for such investigations remain limited to date.

pmc-10634158.title: Prognostic impact of severe neutropenia in colorectal cancer patients treated with TAS-102 and bevacizumab, addressing immortal-time bias
pmc-10634158.creator: Daichi Watanabe, Hironori Fujii, Koichi Ohata, Hirotoshi Iihara, Akitaka Makiyama, Ryo Kobayashi, Chiemi Hirose, Shiori Hishida, Serika Matsuoka, Jesse Yu Tajima, Shigeru Kiyama, Takao Takahashi, Akio Suzuki, Nobuhisa Matsuhashi
pmc-10634158.description: BackgroundSeveral studies have reported an association between severe neutropenia and long-term survival in patients treated with trifluridine-tipiracil (TAS-102). Because some of these studies failed to address immortality time bias, however, their findings should be interpreted with caution. Additionally, the association between severe neutropenia and survival in patients receiving TAS-102 in combination with bevacizumab (Bmab) remains unclear.

pmc-10636105.title: Selective dopamine D2 receptor deletion from Nkx6.2 expressing cells causes impaired cognitive, motivation and anxiety phenotypes in mice
pmc-10636105.creator: Lucila Bechelli, Eugenia Tomasella, Sofia Lopez Cardoso, Martina Belmonte, Diego M Gelman
pmc-10636105.description: Abnormal dopamine neurotransmission is a common trait of some psychiatric diseases, like schizophrenia or bipolar disorder. Excessive dopaminergic tone in subcortical brain regions is associated with psychotic episodes, while reduced prefrontal dopaminergic activity is associated with impaired cognitive performance and reduced motivation, among other symptoms.

pmc-10736353.title: PSYCHOSOCIAL FACTORS AND NONCOMMUNICABLE DISEASES IN OLDER SUB-SAHARA AFRICANS
pmc-10736353.creator: James Muruthi, Margaret Adamek
pmc-10736353.description: Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) has the fastest-growing proportion of older individuals globally. Concurrently, non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are a growing burden in the SSA aging population. An essential step towards reducing NCDs is an enhanced understanding of the various diseases and discussing their psychosocial risk factors.

pmc-11330448.title: A method for extracting buildings from remote sensing images based on 3DJA-UNet3+
pmc-11330448.creator: Yingjian Li, Yonggang Li, Xiangbin Zhu, Haojie Fang, Lihua Ye
pmc-11330448.description: Building extraction aims to extract building pixels from remote sensing imagery, which plays a significant role in urban planning, dynamic urban monitoring, and many other applications. UNet3+ is widely applied in building extraction from remote sensing images. However, it still faces issues such as low segmentation accuracy, imprecise boundary delineation, and the complexity of network models.

pmc-12584796.title: A Concise Review of the Approved MET TKIs (Savolitinib, Gumarontinib, Vebreltinib, Tepotinib, Capmatinib) in China for MET Exon 14 Splice Site Mutated (METex14+) NSCLC Circa 2025
pmc-12584796.creator: Yanyan Hu, Sai-Hong Ignatius Ou
pmc-12584796.description: Splice site mutations around or within exon 14 of MET (METex14+) are rare, but are one of the common actionable driver mutations in elderly patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Globally, only two MET tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), both Type Ib (capmatinib and tepotinib), have been approved in a single Phase 2 trial.

pmc-12714526.title: Rare Case of Metastatic Melanoma With Biventricular Cardiac Involvement
pmc-12714526.creator: Mohammed Najdat Seijari, Bana Sabbagh, Taraneh Zamani, Mohamad Hijazi, Godbless Ajenaghughrure, Fayaz Khan, Kamal Shemisa
pmc-12714526.description: BackgroundMelanoma is an aggressive skin cancer with rising global incidence and potential for widespread metastasis, including to the heart. Cardiac involvement is rare, and standardized diagnostic and management strategies remain undefined.Case SummaryWe present a patient with biventricular cardiac metastases from melanoma. Multimodal imaging—including transesophageal echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and positron emission tomography–computed tomography—was essential in identifying cardiac tumor burden.

pmc-13093578.title: Barriers to Occupational and Physical Therapy Utilization for Children With Cancer
pmc-13093578.creator: Maria C. Swartz, Shiming Zhang, Donna Kelly, Clark R. Andersen, Keri Schadler, Alakh P. Rajan, Eduardo Gonzalez Villarreal, Stephanie J. Wells, Amy Heaton, Karen Moody
pmc-13093578.description: IntroductionOccupational and physical therapy (OT/PT) referrals and utilization barriers for childhood cancer patients have not been adequately examined. The current study investigated factors influencing referrals to and utilization of OT/PT services among children with cancer at an NIH‐designated cancer center.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included pediatric cancer patients (up to 18.99 years) presenting to the center over a 33.5‐month period.

pmc-13286633.title: The dual face of lamin A/C cardiomyopathy: risk prediction of heart failure and arrhythmias
pmc-13286633.creator: Stephane Heymans
pmc-13286633.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Graphical Abstract Graphical AbstractFor image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text. This editorial refers to ‘Laminopathies: natural history and risk prediction of heart failure’, by P. Charron et al., https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehag104. Depending on the perspective and clinical focus, lamin A/C-related cardiomyopathy (LMNA-CMP) has traditionally been viewed either as a predominantly arrhythmogenic disorder or as a severe form of dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM). This apparent dichotomy reflects the true dual nature of laminopathies.

pmc-13464419.title: Nitrogen-doped rGO-supported 2D MnO2 catalysts for improved CO2 electroreduction
pmc-13464419.creator: Abhishek Dhasmana, Sravendra Rana, Jagriti, Ajay, Pravin P. Ingole, Soni Mishra, Sumant Upadhyay, Abhishek K. Mishra
pmc-13464419.description: Nitrogen-doped reduced graphene oxide (NrGO), manganese dioxide (MnO2), and a composite (NrGO–MnO) were synthesized via hydrothermal treatment, where the confined hydrothermal conditions facilitate controlled nucleation and anisotropic two-dimensional growth. Structural and morphological analyses confirmed the formation of poorly crystalline MnO fragments uniformly dispersed on the NrGO framework, effectively preventing graphene restacking and enhancing surface accessibility.

pmc-13482510.title: Social capital in health research ‒ Conceptual model of disease-specific social capital based on disease-specific social networks
pmc-13482510.creator: Ulla-Sisko Lehto, Markku Ojanen, Taina Turpeenniemi-Hujanen
pmc-13482510.description: ObjectivesSocial capital is a resource derived from human social structure comprising social networks and their cognitive contents, such as values and norms, e.g., trust. These are old psychological concepts, but psychological theories and conceptualization are often ignored in studying social capital in public health research.Study designA narrative review-based analysis of the components of social capital from a psychological perspective.

pmc-13679550.title: Green Nanoparticles in Precision Agriculture: A Critical Review of Smart Crop Management, Nano-Enabled Delivery Systems, and Sustainable Farming
pmc-13679550.creator: Abisha Meji Marshal Williams, Milon Selvam Dennison, Sarad Pawar Naik Bukke, Bosco Christin Maria Arputham Ashwin
pmc-13679550.description: Sustainable agricultural production requires approaches that improve resource-use efficiency while limiting environmental burdens. This critical review examines green-synthesized Nanoparticles (NPs) in precision agriculture, covering sustainable synthesis, smart crop management, nano-enabled delivery systems, nano-biosensors, plant-nanoparticle interactions, environmental risks, circular agriculture, and digital technologies.
